During the conversation, Tajani stressed the need to respect Libya's sovereignty and not to extend the Ukraine war, the sources said. (ANSA). Read article...

items.t: Poland accuses Russia of violating airspace with drone
items.m: A Russian reconnaissance drone briefly entered Polish airspace during an attack on Ukraine overnight in an incident just days after three Russian missiles fell on Polish territory, the army and ministers said.

items.m: Zelensky urged Ukraine’s allies to step up supplies of interceptors for Patriot air defence systems.

items.t: Narrow majority of Germans oppose military aid to Ukraine in survey
items.m: Nov 24 - A narrow majority of Germans oppose giving military aid to Kyiv as Russia wages war in Ukraine, a reversal from a year ago, according to a survey published by the nonprofit organisation Koerber Stiftung on Tuesday.

items.t: Russia-Ukraine war live: Kyiv says attacks on ships off Libya self-defence
items.m: Kyiv responds to criticism after claiming responsibility for attacking a Russian warship and a cargo vessel off Libya.

items.t: ‘We’ll keep sinking Russian ships’: Ukraine challenges Putin’s global reach
items.m: Ukraine's strike off Libya signals Kyiv's ability to challenge Russian influence beyond the front lines.

items.t: Is North Korea holding back on sending Russia more troops?
items.m: A North Korean troop buildup Ukraine warned about months ago has yet to materialize, even as strategic cooperation continues. Analysts say Pyongyang is balancing its ties with Moscow and Beijing.

items.t: Red lines, political horse-trading and Ukraine: Inside the EU's increasingly bitter budget battle
items.m: EU capitals are divided on several fronts ahead of key talks on the bloc's next long-term budget: overall size, political priorities, Ukraine financing and new EU taxes. Tense domestic politics make compromise harder, with only leaders expected to break the deadlock.

items.t: Russian governor suspected of orchestrating scheme to embezzle and funnel a billion rubles abroad reportedly offers to resign and fight in Ukraine
items.m: The Meshchansky Court in Moscow will soon rule on a pretrial restriction for Andrey Chibis, the governor of the Murmansk region, the Russian business news outlet RBC and the Russian business daily Kommersant reported, citing sources. Investigators plan to seek his arrest, according to the outlets.

items.t: UK bought fake C4 explosives for Ukraine, FT investigation finds
items.m: Britain has for several years bought tons of explosives for Ukraine from an American company that marketed the product as an improved version of the military explosive C4, a Financial Times investigation found. However, tests later showed the material contained no RDX, the key component of standard C4.

items.t: Merz to meet Pope Leo, Meloni in Rome
items.m: The German chancellor and Pope Leo are expected to discuss human dignity, AI and Ukraine.

items.t: Ukraine insists attack on Russian ships in Libya was self-defence
items.m: KYIV, Nov 24 - Ukraine's foreign minister said on Tuesday a drone attack against a Russian military vessel and cargo ship in Libyan waters at the weekend was a legitimate act of self-defence, following criticism from the government in Tripoli.

items.t: UK warns of Russian sabotage threat to companies that supply Ukraine
items.m: LONDON, Nov 24 - Britain's defence ministry and domestic spy agency MI5 on Tuesday issued a warning to companies providing direct support to Ukraine's military that they faced an increased sabotage threat from Russia.

items.t: Could Russia-Ukraine war threaten Libya’s fragile reunification process?
items.m: Ukraine's involvement in Libya raises concerns as Zelenskyy admits targeting Russian vessels in a key port city.

items.t: At least 490,000 Russian soldiers killed in Ukraine, Rosstat data leak reveals
items.m: Two hacking groups extracted the data from the statistics agency's systems on 1 November. The figure comes from death certificates registered up to the end of August, so it excludes missing servicemen and deaths not yet recorded.

items.t: Russia tows it cargo ship back home after Ukrainian drone attack
items.m: The Russian cargo ship Sparta II was towed back to home waters after a Ukrainian drone attack in the Gulf of Finland

items.t: Leaked data suggests 500,000 Russian soldiers killed since start of Ukraine invasion
items.m: More than 500,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in the war with Ukraine, according to an estimate by a number of media organisations. The figures are based on a huge dataset that was hacked from Russia’s state statistics agency Rosstat by Belarusian activist group Cyber Partisans and a Ukrainian hacker group, Silent Crow. Two independent Russian news outlets Meduza and Mediazona say the death toll may rise to more than 700,000 once missing soldiers are included.

items.t: Ex- Ukraine prosecutor general accuses Zelenskyy's office of interfering in anti-corruption investigation
items.m: Former prosecutor general Ruslan Kravchenko alleges political interference, while Zelenskyy defended his removal and anti-corruption agencies rejected the accusations.

items.t: Ukraine invokes U.N. Charter in defense of its strike on Russian warship in Libya
items.m: Kyiv says the strike on the Russian corvette Merkuriy off the coast of Libya did not expand the war’s geographic scope but was simply an exercise of Ukraine’s lawful right to self-defense. Ukraine “isn’t dragging anyone into the war or spreading it anywhere else,” Foreign Ministry spokesperson Heorhii Tykhyi said Tuesday.

items.t: Zelensky Confirms Ukraine Was Behind Drone Attack on Russian Cargo Ship in Gulf of Finland
items.m: Volodymyr Zelensky said the cargo ship Sparta II and "every vessel with a Russian flag" are legitimate targets for Ukrainian strikes.

items.t: Explainer-Libya's messy frozen conflict
items.m: Nov 24 - Ukraine's sinking of a Russian naval vessel in a Libyan port on Sunday showed how a long-paralysed conflict in the North African country, involving a number of regional powers, risks triggering fresh outbreaks of instability.

items.t: Ukraine needs $160 billion in external support in 2027, Zelensky says

items.m: Finnish, Estonian and Russian vessels took part in a joint rescue operation to put out the fire.

items.t: Zimbabwean convicted in South Africa of trying to fight in Ukraine
items.m: Hundreds of people from different African countries have been recruited to fight for Russia, according to Ukraine.

items.t: After Libya, where will Ukraine strike Russia next?
items.m: From Libya to Sudan and Mali, Ukraine is targeting Russia's military networks across Africa.

items.t: Ukraine's bid for NATO membership and more air defense remain controversial
items.m: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is calling for the rapid acceptance of his country into NATO. However, the necessary unanimity for this is lacking, as shown during the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin.

items.m: The warning follows a fresh wave of security incidents across Europe in recent weeks, including airspace violations and reported cyber and sabotage attacks.

items.t: Italy watches worryingly as Ukraine strikes Russian boats in Libya
items.m: Ukraine's naval drone strikes on two Russian vessels in and off Benghazi have alarmed Italy, amid fears that the attacks could reignite Libya's civil war.

items.t: Zelensky says he’ll ask new U.S. Congress to tighten sanctions on Russia if Trump fails to secure peace deal by year’s end
items.m: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky told Bloomberg he will ask the new U.S. Congress to increase pressure on Russia if Donald Trump fails to get Vladimir Putin to end the war on terms acceptable to Kyiv by the end of the year.

items.m: Several Russian regions have introduced restrictions on retail sales of gasoline and diesel following a renewed spate of Ukrainian attacks on oil refineries.

items.t: A leak from Russia’s federal statistics agency made it possible to estimate the country’s military death toll in the war against Ukraine. What else did it reveal?
items.m: At least 700,000 Russian service members have died in the war against Ukraine. Journalists from Meduza and Mediazona reached that figure using data that the hacker groups Belarusian Cyber Partisans and Silent Crow obtained when they broke into a database belonging to Rosstat, Russia’s federal statistics agency. It’s the first estimate to include service members listed as missing. Other researchers have also studied the hacked Rosstat data. Here’s what they found.

items.t: Russian losses on Ukrainian front top 700,000 including missing
items.m: New analysis of leaked Russian government data suggests more than 700,000 Russian soldiers have died in the war against Ukraine. Independent Russian media outlets have updated their estimates of Moscow's military casualties, including soldiers missing on the frontline, after Belarusian and Ukrainian hackers obtained figures from the Russian statistics agency. FRANCE 24's Carys Garland explains.

items.t: Libya’s Haftar visits Turkiye days after Ukraine hits Russian warship
items.m: Ahead of Erdogan’s Libya trip, Haftar’s visit suggests Turkiye seeks another way to bring the country's rivals together.

items.t: 'It's simply cheaper to fund Ukraine': Ukrainian economist warns Europe against cutting aid to Kyiv
items.m: Cutting financial support for Kyiv risks emboldening Moscow and exposing Europe to further Russian aggression, Tymofiy Mylovanov told Euronews. He warned that forcing Ukraine into concessions without credible security guarantees could pave the way for another war.

items.t: Putin says Ukraine hits Russian oil plants despite Trump’s requests, promises retaliation
items.m: MOSCOW, Nov 24 - Ukraine has continued attacks on Russian oil refineries despite requests from US President Donald Trump to refrain, Russian leader Vladimir Putin said on Tuesday, pledging to retaliate.

items.t: Ukrainian psyop radio mixes Russian rock with instructions on how to surrender, NYT reports
items.m: Ukraine’s Special Operations Forces run a network of radio transmitters that they use to wage psychological warfare against Russian troops, The New York Times reported. The transmitters air different programs tailored to conditions in each sector of the front line. The programs sound like local radio, except that the music and news alternate with instructions on how to surrender.

items.t: Hackers and media outlets expose what the Kremlin tried to hide: At least 500,000 dead on the Ukrainian front
items.m: Since Russian troops invaded Ukraine in February 2022, Vladimir Putin has blocked the publication of casualty figures. However, hackers have breached the records of Rosstat, the Russian federal statistics agency, and exiled media outlets have thoroughly examined the data. The death toll could exceed 700,000 if missing soldiers are included.

items.t: Belarus's Lukashenko proposes flying with Ukraine's Zelenskiy to Moscow for talks
items.m: Nov 24 - Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko, a close ally of Russian leader Vladimir Putin, proposed in an interview published on Tuesday that he and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy fly together to Moscow for Kremlin talks to end the war in Ukraine.

items.t: South Africa convicts Zimbabwean who tried to fight Ukraine for Russia
items.m: The Zimbabwean man was arrested on November 8 at a Johannesburg airport while attempting to board a flight to Russia.

items.m: Ukraine will need €115 billion in external financing next year to sustain its economy and war effort against Russia, President Volodymyr Zelensky said Tuesday, adding that Kyiv had secured commitments for about €90 billion from the European Union.

items.t: Ukraine says attack on Russian ships in Libya was self-defense
items.m: Both Russian naval vessels and cargo ships transporting military equipment were valid targets, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha says.

items.m: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said his country was behind attacks that sank a Russian warship and damaged a sanctioned cargo vessel off Libya.

items.t: Russian strike kills two people in Ukraine's Odesa region, governor says
items.m: Nov 24 - A Russian strike has killed two people and injured three more, including a child, in Ukraine's Black Sea region of Odesa, hitting cars and private and industrial buildings, Governor Oleh Kiper said on Telegram late on Tuesday.

items.t: Ukraine Attack Off Coast of Libya Shows Reach of Its Naval Drones
items.m: President Volodymyr Zelensky said that Ukrainian drones had sunk a corvette and hit a dry cargo vessel, in attacks that involved special operations forces.

items.t: China calls for normal flow of key livelihood supplies in Black Sea
items.m: A Chinese envoy on Monday called for ensuring the normal flow of essential supplies for people's livelihoods in the Black Sea, as the Ukraine crisis continues to drag on and hostilities keep escalating.
